subject: GravityWorks multi-year term assurance — exec clearance request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Kahn <skahn@gravityworks.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: GravityWorks multi-year terms — initial ask

Samira — thanks again for the thoughtful discussion yesterday. As promised, attaching a consolidated summary and the latest quote (quote-v3.xlsx) with the proposed 3-year structure. High level: 3-year committed term with a price-lock on the per-token rates and two protection clauses you asked about.

Key commercial asks for exec review (summary attached):
- Price lock: maintain today's rates for 36 months on agreed SKUs (no mid-term price increases).
- Uplift cap: annual uplift capped at 3% per year (applied to list rate on anniversary).
- Renewal protection: at renewal, Redwood may propose an adjustment up to 5% unless GravityWorks increases committed spend by >=30% YoY or converts to a dedicated pool; otherwise renewal adjustment capped at 5%.

The procurement team is asking for our formal internal approval for the non-standard uplift cap + renewal guard language before they sign. They also flagged two legal redlines in the redlines file.

Attachments: GravityWorks_MultiYear_Term_Summary.pdf, quote-v3.xlsx, redlines-GrvWks-20261129.docx

Ask: can deal desk/execs confirm whether leadership can approve the 3% uplift cap + 5% renewal cap for this account (Deal ID: DW-202611-9821)? GravityWorks is a strategic target in our enterprise pipeline and asked for clarity this week.

Thanks — I captured the specific bullets in the summary to make approvals quick.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GravityWorks multi-year terms — initial ask

Karthik — thanks for the packet. Quick read and a few questions before I can sign off:

1) Commercial risk: the 3% annual cap seems reasonable for a strategic customer, but we need a guardrail that the cap only applies to the negotiated SKUs and usage bands. Please make that explicit in the summary.
2) Renewal protection: the 5% cap at renewal is acceptable as a baseline, but I want a clause that allows Redwood to reprice when our unit economics materially change (e.g., a new model generation that materially increases costs). Can legal propose a trigger definition (e.g., >20% cost delta or new model class)?
3) Approval authority: Jordan, do you want this routed to Deal Desk Ops or do you want exec-level signoff (we can approve up to a 3% annual cap; renewal cap >3% needs a documented exec exception)?

If Jordan prefers exec clearance, I'm fine approving contingent on the above clarifications and a capped credit liability (max credit exposure: $150k).

— Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Kahn <skahn@gravityworks.com>, procurement@gravityworks.com
Date: 2026-11-30T13:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GravityWorks multi-year terms — initial ask

Laura — thanks, good points. I've uploaded a tightened summary (attached) that:
- Limits the 3% uplift cap to the listed SKUs/usage bands and includes examples of how it applies.
- Adds a business-cost-trigger paragraph for renewal repricing: Redwood may reprice at renewal if underlying inference SG&A or GPU-cost indices increase >20% between the effective date and renewal; legal will draft a specific definition for "material cost delta."
- Calls out a credit exposure cap of $150k as suggested.

Jordan — tagging you for decision: per our authority matrix, does this need exec-level signoff? We are in front of a procurement deadline on Friday and Samira has been explicit about needing contractual language now. If we need exec signoff, can we route to Jordan + Aditya for quick clearance?

I copied GravityWorks so they see we're moving quickly and to avoid rework.

Attachments: redlines-GrvWks-20261129.docx (updated)

— Karthik

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: GravityWorks multi-year terms — initial ask

Karthik / team — reviewed the latest. Exec clearance granted with the following explicit constraints (document these in the SOW and final MSA):

1) Approve: 3-year term, 3% annual uplift cap on listed SKUs/usage bands only.
2) Approve: Renewal protection with a 5% renewal cap, provided the customer does not increase committed spend by >=30% YoY.
3) Condition: We will include a narrowly-defined cost-trigger carve (as discussed) that allows Redwood to reopen pricing at renewal if inference cost indices rise >20%. Legal to propose exact metric language.
4) Condition: Credit exposure limit capped at $150,000. Any credit or rebate beyond that requires CFO sign-off.
5) Escalation path: If GravityWorks requests a waiver to any of the above (e.g., expansion that triggers different economics), route back to Jordan+Laura for re-eval.

Karthik — you have exec sign-off. Please update the SOW and send back to legal for clean MSA language. Aditya, please prepare a short internal memo quantifying the max theoretical liability under these terms for our finance partner.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Deal Desk & Pricing
